headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage and cascading error: Perplexity ingests uploaded docs and browsing context while Dagster is a non-executing orchestrator with no host I/O, so the pair mainly risks unsafe handoff and shared-context…

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no clipboard, filesystem, MCP, or network I/O, so it cannot directly ingest Perplexity output by default. Perplexity does ingest uploaded documents and browsing context, but the pair lacks a documented automatic bridge. The only plausible pathway is manual copy-paste or user-mediated transfer, so blast radius is small.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies Perplexity text into Dagster task definitions or docs, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF a shared file or message bridge is added between the agents, the pathway becomes direct.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste Perplexity outputs into Dagster configs without review.
Use a plain-text sanitizer before any manual transfer.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to any shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Perplexity touches search queries, uploaded documents, and browsing context, while Dagster is a data-engineering orchestrator with no host execution or file access. The pair can still leak sensitive content if users move documents or query text from Dagster workflows into Perplexity for analysis. The interaction is plausible in default usage, but not automatic.
conditions: IF Dagster outputs contain sensitive records and are uploaded into Perplexity, those records enter vendor-hosted processing.
IF the same user account is used to search or upload confidential material in Perplexity, leakage scope expands across sessions.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to Perplexity.
Redact secrets from Dagster outputs first.
Use separate accounts for sensitive and non-sensitive work.
Avoid uploading raw pipeline artifacts to Perplexity.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on exported files.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write files, modify git state, or run subprocesses, while Perplexity is vendor-hosted and also cannot write the host filesystem. Their write surfaces do not overlap, so direct resource contention is minimal. Any conflict would require an external orchestrator or shared mutable resource not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF an external system gives both agents write access to the same repository or directory, conflicts can emerge.
IF the operator adds shared OAuth scopes or a shared database, contention risk increases.
mitigations: Keep write targets separate.
Avoid shared git repositories for both agents.
Use explicit locking in any external orchestrator.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity produces cited answers from browsing context, and Dagster is a data orchestrator that could consume those outputs as inputs to pipelines or docs. If Dagster treats Perplexity text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream work products. Dagster does not verify external claims by itself, so the pathway exists without a built-in guard.
conditions: IF Dagster pipelines or runbooks are generated from Perplexity answers without human verification, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF Perplexity citations are copied into automated Dagster artifacts, downstream consumers may trust them uncritically.
mitigations: Require human review before using Perplexity outputs in Dagster artifacts.
Cross-check claims against primary sources.
Mark AI-generated text as untrusted in workflow templates.
Use a verification checklist for any copied citations.
requires-engineering: add automated source validation.

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted and processes search queries, uploaded documents, and browsing context, while Dagster touches no data classes in the profile. No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented between them, so compliance risk is limited to general policy handling of whatever the operator uploads into Perplexity.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into Perplexity, the operator must ensure the vendor policy permits that transfer.
IF Dagster outputs include data subject records, retention and residency rules must be checked before upload.
mitigations: Do not upload regulated data without approval.
Review Perplexity privacy and retention settings.
Keep Dagster outputs de-identified before sharing.
Document the allowed data classes for each workflow.
